system:
You write CANON ENTRIES for an illustrated edition of a work of literature. A canon entry fixes the identity of one character, location or object so that independently generated images agree with each other. Return only JSON matching the schema.

Rules:
- The work's text is binding: anything it says about appearance must be in the entry.
- Where the text is silent, follow the work's widely known visual tradition if one exists; otherwise invent a look that fits the era and the work brief. Never contradict the text.
- Each entry's `text` is one prompt-ready paragraph of at most 500 characters, starting with the name and a colon.
  - character (people, beings, animals, groups): age range; build; skin; hair and beard; facial notes; one signature outfit (the one worn most often) and its colours; signature props the figure carries alone. For a group, describe a typical member.
  - location: terrain; architecture; vegetation; landmarks. No people.
  - object: form; material; colour.
- Fix only identity. Leave out poses, expressions, actions, weather, time of day, other people (attendants, companions, crowds) and anything that compares the figure with someone else.
- STAGES: almost every entry has exactly ONE stage. A character gets a second stage only when the text itself says they have aged from child to adult or adult to elder across the work; a location only when the text says it was built, destroyed or rebuilt. Different scenes, days, rooms, moods or events are NOT stages. At most three. Objects always have exactly one stage. Each stage is a complete entry on its own.
- Obey the work brief's depiction rules: if a rule limits how this entry may be shown, write only the permitted showing.
- `quotes`: short passages (under 120 characters, copied exactly) the entry relied on, each with the id of the unit it comes from. Only quote units you were given.
- `source`: text, tradition, invention, or mixed.
content: {"id":"the_disciples","kind":"character","stages":[{"id":"the_disciples_s1","label":"The Twelve and the companions of Jesus","when":"First-century Galilee and Judea, the years of Jesus' ministry","text":"The disciples: Jewish men of Galilee aged roughly 20 to 40; sturdy fishermen's build, weathered tanned Mediterranean skin, dark to olive-brown hair and short beards; faces lined by sun and work. Signature outfit: a plain undyed linen tunic of earth brown under a wool mantle of faded blue-grey with tassel fringes, leather sandals. Signature props: none carried alone; the fishermen's nets and boat belong to the scene.","source":"mixed","quotes":[{"unit":"matthew-10-2","quote":"Now the names of the twelve apostles are these."},{"unit":"john-21-4","quote":"Jesus stood on the beach; yet the disciples didn't know that it was Jesus."}]}]}

stages.label: The Twelve and the companions of Jesus
stages.when: First-century Galilee and Judea, the years of Jesus' ministry
stages.text: The disciples: Jewish men of Galilee aged roughly 20 to 40; sturdy fishermen's build, weathered tanned Mediterranean skin, dark to olive-brown hair and short beards; faces lined by sun and work. Signature outfit: a plain undyed linen tunic of earth brown under a wool mantle of faded blue-grey with tassel fringes, leather sandals. Signature props: none carried alone; the fishermen's nets and boat belong to the scene.

quotes.quote: Now the names of the twelve apostles are these.
Jesus stood on the beach; yet the disciples didn't know that it was Jesus.
